prompt:
Use case: style-transfer. Create ONE QUEEN OF SPADES for the exact same Design 2 playing-card deck as the supplied APPROVED King of Spades. The supplied image is the authoritative layout, figure-scale, painted style, frame and floral reference.
PRESERVE: full card 5:7 portrait about 1060x1484; black-and-gold narrow lotus-vine outer frame, ivory rounded edge, beaded gold rules, two diagonal ivory index panels, richly dense Chinese lotus floral fields on black ground, shaped antique-white reserve with fine gold tracery, diagonal interlocked robe join and SMALL central turquoise jewel. Same reduced head/torso scale and broad sleeve silhouette spanning the inner sides. Generous dense floral surround. No enlarged portrait or emptier background. Retain exact pattern scale and placement wherever the changed figure permits.
REPLACE the King with a dignified adult Chinese royal woman, distinct elegant naturalistic face, warm skin, composed intelligent expression, face gently toward VIEWER'S RIGHT with BOTH EYES visible. No facial hair. Black hair neatly dressed into an upswept court coiffure. Instead of the King's black cap, a compact MING-INSPIRED PHOENIX CROWN: rounded gold filigree structure, teal-blue inlay, small gold phoenix and dragon ornaments, pearls and red stones, short delicate pearl pendants at temples. Inspired by Ming phoenix crowns preserved in the Palace Museum; stylized to fit the deck, NOT an exact reconstruction. Crown must be contained below the inner top rule with breathing room, not huge or tall. No European leaf-point crown, Tudor hood, Qing fan-shaped headdress, Japanese costume or fantasy tiara.
COSTUME: graceful broad-sleeved madder-red silk robe with delicate gold phoenix and cloud embroidery, ivory inner collar, dark teal embroidered shoulder/stole bands inspired by xiapei, antique-gold borders and lotus cuffs matching the deck. Refined pearl earrings. The red/teal/gold costume complements the Kings' yellow robes; it must feel purpose-designed for the Queen, not a face swap on the King's dragon tunic. Covered formal court dress, natural drapery, narrower graceful shoulders with flowing wide sleeves.
SPADES ATTRIBUTE: replace sword with a slender gold ceremonial SCEPTER on viewer's RIGHT. Modest jade-and-gold cloud/lotus finial, clearly a blunt ceremonial staff with NO BLADE and NO POINT. One natural hand grips it at chest height, the other lightly gathers the robe at the upper chest. Both hands well formed. Scepter tip around y=17% of canvas, comfortably within inner frame. No orb or weapon.
INDICES: black serif Q above a plain black spade in upper-left panel, exact 180-degree rotated counterpart bottom-right. Clear Q tail contained within the panel. No K, no extra text.
TWO-WAY: exactly two opposing waist-up portraits of THE SAME woman. Lower figure, face, crown, scepter, hands, robes, flowers and indices are precise 180-degree rotated counterparts of the upper, seamlessly joined around the center jewel. Same age, face and pose on both ends. All objects stay within the inner border.
Match the King's fine warm outlines, subtly shaded naturalism and luminous printed-silk illustration; no photo, anime, cartoon, 3D render, extra limbs, scene, mockup, watermark or labels. One complete card image.
